terms.definition: The record an electronic lock keeps of every credential that opened it and when, downloaded with a programmer. The first objective evidence in a room entry or theft case.
The signed, unbroken record of who held an item of evidence, when, and what they did with it, from collection to court. A gap lets anyone say the evidence was changed.
The Veldane LP stance: officers observe, report and de-escalate. Physical intervention, searches and detention happen only as policy and local law allow.
A question that invites an account ("walk me through...") rather than a yes or no. It gets more information and does not suggest the answer.
Saying or implying the hotel is at fault or will pay. Liability is decided by claims, insurers and counsel on the facts, never on the floor.
Matching a person to the room registration (photo ID, name, registration details) before issuing a key, opening a door or confirming a guest is staying.
Lowering tension with calm voice, open body language, listening, clear requests and options, so a conflict ends without force.
A key or card that opens every room in a section, floor or building. Its loss puts every room it opens at risk until the locks are re-keyed or the card is cancelled.
An alarm raised when a controlled door stays open past its set time. A response checks the door, the area and the CCTV, and records who left it open and why.
The numbered two-part ticket that ties stored luggage to its owner. Bags are released only against the matching half, or against verified identity and a signed release.
Counting every issued key and card against the register at set times, so a missing one is found the same day rather than after a loss.
How long recordings are kept before the system overwrites them. Footage for an incident must be exported and preserved before that time runs out.
A digital fingerprint (for example SHA-256) taken when footage is exported. A matching hash later shows the copy was not changed.
A bag or package left with no owner in sight. Don't touch it: ask nearby people, check CCTV for who left it, keep people back and follow the suspicious item plan if it isn't explained.
Changing a lock, or its electronic code, so old keys and cards no longer work. The cost is doors x cost per door, plus labour, plus new keys (KcLpMath RekeyCost).
Checking the panel, going to the zone with a radio, and confirming fire or a false alarm within the time the fire plan sets, while the building's evacuation rules apply.
Any time a sprinkler, alarm or other fire system is out of service. It needs a permit, a fire watch, notice to the insurer and the fire authority as required, and a restore check.
A trained person patrolling an area with a working means to raise the alarm while its fire protection is impaired, on a set route and logged.
The money set aside for what a claim is still expected to cost: estimated medical, indemnity and expense, less what has already been paid (KcLpMath ClaimReserve).
What a claim has cost and is expected to cost in total: paid plus reserve (KcLpMath ClaimIncurred).
Written permission for welding, cutting or grinding, with checks before work, a fire watch during and after, and sign-off when the area is safe.
A fair, documented inquiry into a complaint: a neutral investigator, interviews of both sides and witnesses, evidence before conclusions, confidentiality and protection from retaliation.
Stock lost without a sale: (expected - actual) / expected x 100 (KcLpMath ShrinkPercent). A rise is a question to investigate, not proof of theft.
The plan that follows an audit finding: fix the cause, not just the symptom, with an owner, a date and a check that it worked.
Post hours per week divided by one person's contracted hours, adjusted for leave and training (KcLpMath FtesRequired).
An immediate, hotel-wide search plan for a missing child: describe, lock down exits, search to a pattern, call the police by the set time.
Keeping a scene as found: nothing touched or moved except to save life, access logged, the area secured until the police release it.
The most people a room may hold, set by the fire authority from its exits and floor area. Exceeding it is a life-safety breach.
Battery or generator lights that switch on when power fails, so people can find exits. Tested monthly and for full duration each year.
Incidents or loss value divided by occupied room nights, times 1,000 (KcLpMath LossRatePer1000RoomNights). It lets hotels of different sizes be compared.
Cancelling every credential, account and code a person holds on the day they leave, and checking it worked.
A card payment reversed by the card issuer after a dispute. A ring of chargebacks with shared details points to fraud, not unhappy guests.
The form kept by every phone that takes calls: exact words, voice, background, time. It is filled in during the call and given to the police.
Leaving a known fact or claim off an insurance proposal. It can let the insurer refuse cover when a claim comes.
Being able to say where every food item came from and where it went, by batch and date, so a suspect product can be found and held.
Signs that someone may be controlled by another person. Staff observe and report to the manager and the police; they never confront or investigate alone.
A claim the evidence does not support. It is handled with facts and the insurer, never with accusations, and the claimant is treated fairly throughout.
Fire-resisting walls and doors that hold fire and smoke in one area. A wedged or opened fire door defeats it.
Expected events per year times the average cost per event (KcLpMath AnnualisedLoss). It is an average, never a worst case.
A written check, before cameras are added, of what they will see, why, who can view it, how long it is kept, and how privacy is protected.
A short, approved first statement in a crisis: what happened, care for those affected, what is being done. No speculation or blame.
Any adverse treatment of someone because they reported a concern or took part in an investigation. Policy forbids it and it is investigated as misconduct.
Fixed times, set against an official forecast or plan, when a crisis team decides what happens next, so decisions aren't put off hoping for better news.
Telling those affected the facts early, openly and repeatedly, with an apology, while counsel shapes the wording, not whether the truth is told.
A cause in the way work is set up (a missing control, an old process) rather than in one person. Post-incident reviews look for these before blaming anyone.
Refusing to serve someone who is intoxicated and looking after them: water, a seat, a safe way home, and a record of what was done.
Automated external defibrillator. In a collapse: call for help and the AED at once, start CPR, and follow the machine's voice prompts until paramedics take over.
